sources.entry: EveryDocs - Simple Document Management System for private use with basic functionality to organize your documents digitally. GPL-3.0 Docker/Ruby

summary.one_liner: EveryDocs Core is the server-side component of EveryDocs, a simple self-hosted document management system for private use that organizes uploaded PDFs.
summary.what_it_does: EveryDocs Core is a Ruby on Rails backend that includes a web interface for managing personal documents. Users upload PDFs with a title, description, and creation date, then organize them into folders and subfolders. Documents can be tagged with people and processing states. The app extracts text from PDFs to support full-text search across titles, descriptions, and content. PDF files can be stored encrypted on disk, though content extraction and full-text search are disabled for encrypted documents. A REST API covers CRUD operations for documents, folders, persons, and processing states, with JsonWebToken authentication.
use_cases: store private PDFs encrypted on disk
track people and processing states on documents
self-hosted document archive with a REST API
access document archive from a mobile browser
how_to_run: SECRET_KEY_BASE="$(openssl rand -hex 64)" docker-compose up --build (from the source folder; uses docker-compose.yaml with database, core, and web containers)
Manual: install Ruby and Rails, download a release, and configure EVERYDOCS_DB_* environment variables
notable: Encrypted PDF storage, enabled per user via a secret_key and a database flag; automatically on for new users after 1.5.0
Full-text search via PDF content extraction
Folder and subfolder organization with people and processing-state tagging
Companion web UI project, EveryDocs Web, referenced in the README
caveats: Anyone who knows the URL can create new accounts, per the README
Encrypted documents get no content extraction and no full-text search
Manual installation is marked as not recommended
